evals.prompt: Deploy SceneScape in ~/deployments/retail-demo with two RTSP cameras and scene name 'Retail Demo'.
evals.expected_output: Deployment completes end-to-end (bootstrap, calibrate, scene phases) without asking clarifying questions, validates the camera inputs, deploys both cameras, and the final response reports DEPLOY COMPLETE with a scene_uid, cross-camera tracking confirmation, and deployment metrics.
assertions: Does not ask clarifying questions since deploy_dir, streams, camera_ids, and scene_name are all explicit in the prompt
Validates that the number of streams matches the number of camera_ids (2 == 2) and that camera_ids are unique before proceeding
Persists deploy-inputs.json via the Step 1 tooling before invoking the orchestrator
Launches the orchestrator script (deploy_scenescape.sh) in an async terminal rather than running steps manually or blocking
Calibration phase produces one calibration JPEG per camera_id
Tracking verification (step 13) confirms tracked objects are associated with more than one camera_id
Final response includes the DEPLOY COMPLETE marker and the Post-Task deployment metrics breakdown

evals.prompt: Continue the SceneScape deployment in ~/deployments/warehouse-demo — it stopped partway through.
evals.expected_output: Agent detects the existing deploy-inputs.json, uses the Fast Path (skips Step 1 questions), and resumes the orchestrator from the step recorded in .deploy-state.json.
assertions: Detects deploy-inputs.json already exists in the deploy_dir and skips re-asking Step 1 questions
Shows the existing streams/camera_ids/scene_name to the user for confirmation instead of silently reusing them
Invokes the orchestrator with only --deploy-dir and --skill-dir (no --fresh)
Resumes from the step recorded in .deploy-state.json rather than restarting from step 1

evals.prompt: In ~/deployments/warehouse-demo, replace cam1 with a new camera at rtsp://192.168.1.15:8554/cam1-new (ID: cam1-new). Redeploy.
evals.expected_output: Agent recognizes the camera/stream change invalidates the Fast Path, re-runs Step 1 in full with the new values, and re-invokes the orchestrator with --fresh.
assertions: Recognizes that a changed stream/camera_id set means this cannot use the Fast Path resume
Re-asks/re-confirms all Step 1 inputs (streams, camera_ids, scene_name) rather than merging partial changes silently
Invokes the orchestrator with --fresh so .deploy-state.json and the old deploy-inputs.json are cleared
Re-runs all phases (bootstrap, calibrate, scene) rather than only the calibration step for the changed camera

evals.prompt: The SceneScape deployment in ~/deployments/warehouse-demo is up, but tracked people keep disappearing and getting new IDs whenever they walk behind a shelf. Can you fix this?
evals.expected_output: Agent recognizes this as a post-deployment tracking-quality complaint, opens only tuning-tracker.md (not tuning-reid.md), asks its questionnaire, then edits tracker-config.json in the deploy_dir and restarts the scene service.
assertions: Does not ask any tuning questions during initial deployment prompts (evals 1-3) — tuning is only triggered by a post-deployment complaint like this one
Identifies the symptom (ID switching during occlusion) as a tracker motion/timing issue and opens tuning-tracker.md, not tuning-reid.md
Asks only the tuning-tracker.md questionnaire, not the full original combined set of questions
Edits the deployed <deploy_dir>/controller/tracker-config.json copy, not the skill's assets/tracker-config.json original
Restarts only the scene service (docker compose up -d --force-recreate scene) rather than re-running the full orchestrator or redeploying from scratch

evals.prompt: The SceneScape deployment in ~/deployments/retail-demo is up, but the same shopper walking from cam1 to cam3 keeps getting a new ID instead of being recognized as the same person. Can you fix this?
evals.expected_output: Agent recognizes this as a post-deployment cross-camera Re-ID complaint, opens only tuning-reid.md (not tuning-tracker.md), asks its questionnaire, then edits reid-config.json in the deploy_dir and restarts the scene service.
assertions: Does not ask any Re-ID tuning questions during initial deployment prompts (evals 1-3) — tuning is only triggered by a post-deployment complaint like this one
Identifies the symptom (identity not preserved across non-overlapping cameras) as a Re-ID issue and opens tuning-reid.md, not tuning-tracker.md
Asks only the tuning-reid.md questionnaire
Edits the deployed <deploy_dir>/controller/reid-config.json copy, not the skill's assets/reid-config.json original
Restarts only the scene service (docker compose up -d --force-recreate scene) rather than re-running the full orchestrator or redeploying from scratch
